pr.title: GVN: Invalidate derefs at loop headers
pr.description:
Fix a miscompiled case I found when re-reviewing rust-lang/rust#132527.

r? cjgillot 
r? oli-obk
pr.author: dianqk

analysis.summary: GVN processes MIR blocks in reverse postorder while caching dereferenced places. For acyclic CFGs reverse postorder is topological, but with loops a cached deref can be stale at a loop header because a not-yet-processed loop-body terminator may have performed an indirect write. The fix computes `maybe_loop_headers` and calls `state.invalidate_derefs()` when visiting each loop header, preventing GVN from reusing the pre-loop deref value across the back edge. The added mir-opt and run-pass tests exercise an enum mutated through `&mut` inside a loop after its field was copied out before the loop.
analysis.originalLogic: GVN walks basic blocks in reverse postorder and maintains a value-numbering state that caches dereferenced places (e.g. `*val_alias`) so later equivalent dereferences can reuse the cached value. The pass implicitly assumes reverse postorder is a valid topological order, so every write that could affect a block has already been processed when the block is visited. In the original code the loop header was visited without invalidating cached derefs.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: At a loop header GVN keeps the deref value numbers cached from before the loop and reuses the dereferenced place/value across the back edge. Since the loop body writes through a possibly-aliasing pointer (the test does `*val = Value::V1;`), the cached deref is no longer valid on the next iteration. In the focused test this allows GVN to replace the loop's aggregate construction `Value::V0(v)` / `_11 = Value::V0(copy _7)`, where `_7` was loaded before the loop from `((*val_alias) as V0).0`, with a copy/re-read of `*val_alias`. After the write the loop then returns the mutated `Value::V1` (or otherwise reads the changed pointee) instead of the `V0(1)` copied before the loop. The corrected output instead invalidates derefs at the loop header and keeps using the copied local.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions containing a loop/back edge where: (1) a dereference such as `*r` is available and cached by GVN before the loop header; (2) the loop body performs an indirect write through a pointer/reference that may alias that dereference (e.g. `*val = Value::V1`); and (3) a value derived from the earlier dereference, or the dereferenced aggregate itself, is used inside the loop or on the loop exit. The test uses `&mut Value`, an opaque `get` returning a shared reborrow, an enum with a discriminant, and a value copied out before the overwrite. The `maybe_loop_headers` helper approximates loop headers for reducible CFGs and explicitly handles self-loops; it can over-approximate, giving conservative invalidation.
analysis.trigger: Visiting a loop header in reverse postorder while GVN still has derefs cached from before the loop, when the loop body (not yet processed) contains an indirect write aliasing the cached deref. In the regression program the header is reached again via the back edge after `*val = Value::V1`, so the cached value of `*val_alias` is stale.
preconditions: The MIR CFG contains at least one back edge / loop header (including a self-loop).
GVN has cached a dereferenced place before reaching the loop header.
The loop body contains an indirect write through a pointer or reference that may alias the cached deref.
A use in the loop or after the loop can be rewritten to use the cached deref value; without invalidation this substitution is unsound across the back edge.
The write is located inside the loop and may not have been processed yet when the header is visited in reverse postorder.
pitfalls: Reverse postorder is not a topological order for loops; assuming it is can leave stale deref value numbers at loop headers.

Borrow-checker aliasing and GVN's deref invalidation are separate concerns. The regression test is well-defined because the value is copied out of `*val_alias` before the mutable write (post-copy overwrite); that does not make the cached deref valid after the write.

Do not conflate the constant-folding seen in the corrected diff (`*val = const Value::V1`) or the `nop`/StorageLive removals with the actual fix; the correctness change is `state.invalidate_derefs()` at loop headers.

The newly added mir-opt test contains misspelled negative directives: `// CEHCK-NOT: copy (*[[VAL_REF]]);`. Those directives are not effective `CHECK-NOT`s, so a focused regression test should spell them correctly or the negative assertion will silently not run.

The `maybe_loop_headers` helper is intentionally a postorder heuristic, not exact dominance; over-marking headers is safe but can reduce optimization. It marks a block visited only after checking successors to handle self-loops.
The helper is shared with JumpThreading in this patch (`loops::maybe_loop_headers`), but the behavioral bug and fix belong to GVN; do not attribute the invalidation change to JumpThreading.
`#[inline(never)]` on `get` helps keep the dereference opaque so GVN cannot simply see through the reborrow.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a MIR-opt test (`tests/mir-opt/gvn_loop.rs`) using `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN` and `// EMIT_MIR gvn_loop.loop_deref_mut.GVN.diff`. Construct an enum `Value` with a discriminant, obtain a shared alias via an `#[inline(never)] fn get<T>(v: &T) -> &T`, destructure `*val_alias` into a local, enter a loop that constructs `Value::V0(v)`, on the second iteration returns it, and on the first iteration writes `*val = Value::V1`. Assert with CHECK lines that the field is loaded once into a local (`[[V]] = copy (((*[[VAL_REF]]) as V0).0: i32)`) and that the loop/return uses `Value::V0(copy [[V]])`; add correctly spelled `CHECK-NOT: copy (*[[VAL_REF]])` guards so GVN cannot substitute a copy/re-read of the dereferenced value. Also add a `-O` `run-pass` UI test (`tests/ui/mir/gvn-loop-miscompile.rs`) asserting the returned value is still `Value::V0(1)` after the loop mutates the pointee. Include a self-loop variant or verify the helper's self-loop marking. No compiler was built here, so no execution or reproduction is claimed.
